body:
In Illinois, painting the outside of a typical 2,000 sq ft home costs about **$3,580 to $9,540** in 2026, or $1.79 to $4.77 per square foot of living area. That is our estimate, built from national prices and what painters in Illinois actually earn: a median of $29.45 an hour, 24% above the national median of $23.75.

| | Illinois | National |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per sq ft of home | $1.79 to $4.77 | $1.50 to $4.00 |
| 2,000 sq ft home | $3,580 to $9,540 | $3,000 to $8,000 |
| Painter median wage | $29.45 an hour | $23.75 an hour |

## Illinois exterior painting cost by home size

| Home size (living area) | Typical cost in Illinois |
| --- | --- |
| 1,500 sq ft | $2,685 to $7,155 |
| 2,000 sq ft | $3,580 to $9,540 |
| 2,500 sq ft | $4,475 to $11,925 |
| 3,000 sq ft | $5,370 to $14,310 |

These are typical ranges for a full repaint with normal prep. A small, simple house with sound paint lands near the low end. Two stories, heavy scraping, wood repairs or premium paint push you toward the top. Enter your own home size and any quote you have in the calculator above.

## Prices in Illinois's largest metro areas

Painter wages are not the same across the state, so neither are prices. Here is the same 2,000 sq ft house in Illinois's major metro areas:

| Metro area | Painter median wage | 2,000 sq ft home |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chicago-Naperville-Elgin | $29.68 | $3,599 to $9,598 |
| Rockford | $34.95 | $4,132 to $11,018 |
| Peoria | $30.98 | $3,731 to $9,948 |
| Springfield | $30.74 | $3,706 to $9,884 |

The gap between Rockford and Chicago-Naperville-Elgin is $5.27 an hour in wages, which works out to roughly $533 to $1,420 on this one job. Small towns and rural areas usually sit closer to the lower metro numbers.

## What affects the price in Illinois

**Siding.** Vinyl siding dominates new homes in the Great Lakes states. In the East North Central region, which includes Illinois, 71% of new single-family homes started in 2025 had vinyl as the main wall material, according to NAHB. Vinyl is often left unpainted, so on a newer vinyl-sided house the paint job may be mostly trim, doors and porches. Older wood-sided houses need scraping, priming and caulking first, which is where the hours go.

**Weather and timing.** Winters here are too cold for exterior paint. Sherwin-Williams says the air, the surface and the paint all need to be at or above 35°F, and the first 48 hours after painting are the critical drying window. In practice that leaves late spring to early fall, which is also when painters are busiest. Booking in late winter for a spring start often gets you a better date, and sometimes a better price.

**Prep.** On older houses, scraping peeling paint, replacing soft boards, caulking and spot-priming can take longer than the painting itself. If two quotes are far apart, compare the prep each one includes before you compare the totals. Our [national guide to exterior painting costs](/blog/cost-to-paint-house-exterior/) covers the other price factors in detail.

## Hiring a painter in Illinois

Licensing for painting-only work is mostly a local matter in Illinois, so ask your city or county building department what applies where you live. Whatever the rules, ask every painter for a certificate of liability insurance, and check that it is current.

If your house was built before 1978, the old paint may contain lead. Under EPA's Renovation, Repair and Painting rule, contractors who disturb that paint must be certified lead-safe and follow containment and cleanup steps. Ask to see the firm's certification before work starts, and expect it to add some cost.

Get at least two or three written quotes that list the same things: which surfaces, how many coats, which paint line, what prep and repairs, and who cleans up. A quote far below the range usually skips prep or uses fewer coats.

## How we worked out these prices

National data from Angi, reported by NerdWallet, puts exterior painting at $1.50 to $4 per square foot of living area. Angi says labor makes up 75% to 95% of a professional paint job. We took 80% as the labor share and adjusted that part by Illinois's painter wage compared with the national median, using Bureau of Labor Statistics 2025 wage data:

**Illinois rate = national rate × (0.2 + 0.8 × $29.45 ÷ $23.75) = national rate × 1.192**

Paint and supplies cost about the same everywhere, so only the labor part moves. Treat the results as a planning range, not a quote. Local demand, the season and each painter's overhead all shift real prices.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to paint a 2,000 sq ft house in Illinois?

About $3,580 to $9,540 for the outside, with most jobs in the middle of that range. In Rockford expect more, about $4,132 to $11,018.

### Where in Illinois is exterior painting most expensive?

Of the metro areas above, Rockford has the highest painter wages at $34.95 an hour, and Chicago-Naperville-Elgin the lowest at $29.68. Prices follow wages because labor is most of the bill.

### When is the best time to paint a house in Illinois?

Late spring to early fall, when the air and walls stay at or above 35°F and you can count on two dry days in a row. Book early: painters fill their calendars by spring.

### Do I need a licensed painter in Illinois?

It depends on your city or county, so ask your local building department. Either way, ask for proof of liability insurance.
